hero.headline: US strikes Iranian radar sites after intercepting drones fired at Bahrain and Kuwait
hero.body:
US and Iran Exchange Military Strikes Over Gulf Region

The United States and Iran engaged in another round of military exchanges on Saturday, with American forces shooting down Iranian drones and striking radar installations, followed by Iranian attacks targeting bases in Kuwait and Bahrain.

Air raid sirens sounded in Bahrain as Iranian ballistic missiles and drones headed toward the Gulf states. Kuwait's military reported intercepting drones and missiles launched at the country. The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attacks as a "serious escalation" and "flagrant violation of its sovereignty," asserting its right to defend itself.

According to the US military's Central Command, Iranian attack drones posed an "immediate threat to regional maritime traffic." In response, American forces shot down four Iranian drones launched toward the Strait of Hormuz and struck Iranian coastal surveillance radar sites on Sirik and Qeshm Island to "defend against further attacks."

Hours later, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had targeted "enemy bases" in the Gulf. The IRGC claimed it fired seven ballistic missiles toward Kuwait and Bahrain. Centcom reported that six missiles were intercepted and a seventh did not reach its target. The command stated there were no reports of harm to US personnel and dismissed Iranian claims of damaging the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain as false.

The escalation marks the latest in a series of tense military encounters that threaten the fragile ceasefire between the two nations. Diplomatic negotiations aimed at ending the conflict have stalled, with both countries calling for changes to any agreement without showing willingness to compromise. US and Iranian negotiators have spent weeks attempting to extend a 60-day ceasefire and initiate new talks on Iran's nuclear program.

President Donald Trump told reporters on Friday that "the situation with Iran seems to be going quite well," while simultaneously stating the US would resolve the matter "very quickly" either through a deal or "the very tough way." Trump faces pressure to end the conflict before midterm elections, citing its negative impact on markets and domestic popularity.

The military exchanges also coincide with regional complications. A ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon's government was announced this week following US-brokered talks, though Iranian-backed Hezbollah rejected the deal. Israeli airstrikes killed nine people in Lebanon on Saturday, including three army soldiers, prompting Lebanon's president to call the strike a "flagrant violation" of sovereignty.

Iran has demanded that any lasting truce extend to Lebanon, complicating efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end broader regional conflict. The continued military tensions have economic ripple effects, with the World Food Programme warning that millions face increased hunger due to soaring energy and food prices connected to the conflict.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St Petersburg in attack Russia calls unprecedented
cards.teaser: Russia urged residents of its second-largest city to stay indoors for the first time since the war began.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck St Petersburg on Saturday, prompting Russian authorities to issue stay-indoors orders to residents—the first such warning since the war began. The attack marked a significant escalation, reaching deep into Russian territory hundreds of miles from the Ukrainian border.

President Putin responded by announcing plans to strengthen Russia's air defenses against the drone attacks. The strikes also disrupted an economic forum being held in Putin's hometown, underscoring the expanding reach of Ukrainian operations within Russian territory.

cards.headline: Chip Sector Selloff Erases $1.3 Trillion in Stock Market Value
cards.teaser: The semiconductor industry suffered a massive selloff on Friday, wiping out more than $1.3 trillion in stock market value in what marked the sector's worst trad.
cards.body:
The semiconductor industry experienced a sharp selloff on Friday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq closing down 4 percent—its largest single-day drop in over a year. The S&P 500 fell 2.6 percent while the Dow declined 1.3 percent. The steep losses came despite positive economic news, as the US added 172,000 jobs in May and maintained an unemployment rate of 4.3 percent.

The selloff highlights growing concerns about whether the AI-driven rally in chip stocks has become overextended. Semiconductor companies have commanded premium valuations based on their role in powering artificial intelligence systems, but the sudden market reversal underscores the volatility when investor sentiment shifts rapidly. Analysts are now evaluating whether this represents profit-taking or signals deeper concerns about the sector's fundamentals.

cards.headline: Screwworm outbreak prompts border closures, hitting Texas cattle industry
cards.body:
A flesh-eating screwworm parasite detected in Texas has prompted Canada to ban cattle imports from the state and triggered concerns across neighboring states. The screwworm, which has not been found in the United States in decades, lays eggs in open wounds on livestock. The larvae then consume living tissue, creating severe injuries that can kill animals if untreated.

Texas cattle ranchers are facing economic losses as international and domestic trade restrictions take effect. Mexico has seen its beef industry benefit from the closure, with increased demand as buyers seek alternative sources. The outbreak comes as ranchers already contend with drought conditions that have strained the industry.

Colorado officials said they are monitoring the situation closely after the parasite was confirmed in Texas. Utah officials also expressed concern about the potential spread of the parasite northward. The screwworm was eradicated from the United States through a decades-long program that released sterile male flies to disrupt breeding cycles.

The current outbreak marks the first detection of the parasite in the country in recent decades, raising questions about how it returned and whether the eradication program needs to be reactivated. Agricultural officials have not yet announced plans for containment or treatment programs.

The economic impact on Texas ranchers could extend beyond immediate trade losses if the outbreak spreads or if additional states and countries impose import restrictions. Screwworm infestations can devastate livestock populations quickly, as the parasites reproduce rapidly in warm climates and can infest any warm-blooded animal with an open wound.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Discusses Possible Government Stake in AI Companies
cards.teaser: President Trump said his administration will explore the U.S. government taking equity positions in artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump said his administration is exploring deals that would allow the American people to benefit from AI company success. The discussions include the possibility of the U.S. government acquiring equity stakes in major artificial intelligence firms like OpenAI.

Trump characterized the concept as potentially "a beautiful thing." The administration has held talks with OpenAI about structuring a government profit-sharing arrangement, with meetings potentially occurring in the near term.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors in Los Angeles have opened an investigation into election fraud allegations in California.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office has launched an investigation into election fraud in California's elections, according to an announcement made as the state's primary races continue to be counted.

The probe follows criticism from conservatives, including President Trump and former Speaker Kevin McCarthy, who have raised questions about California's vote-counting process. McCarthy expressed concerns that California voters were losing confidence in the election process as results continued to arrive from the primary.

cards.headline: Israeli troops kill seven-month-old in West Bank shooting
cards.teaser: A baby was shot dead after Israeli soldiers opened fire on a vehicle, Palestinian officials said.
cards.body:
Israeli troops killed a seven-month-old boy in the occupied West Bank after a soldier opened fire on a vehicle. The Israeli military stated that troops perceived the vehicle accelerating toward them. However, the child's grandmother, who was in the car, disputed this account of events.

A funeral was held for the infant, during which his shrouded body was wrapped in a Palestinian flag and carried by his father to the graveyard. The incident has drawn renewed attention to the use of force by Israeli troops operating in the West Bank.

cards.headline: Protests in Albania over Kushner-backed luxury resort on protected beach
cards.teaser: Days of demonstrations have erupted over plans for a resort linked to Jared Kushner on a pristine coastline.
cards.body:
Albanians have demonstrated against a planned luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner on the Adriatic coast. The project, involving Ivanka Trump, would be built in one of the Mediterranean's most environmentally sensitive areas, drawing opposition from local residents and conservationists.

The protests have sparked concern among European Union officials. Demonstrators argue the resort threatens the protected coastal environment and have directed criticism at both the Trump family and Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth criticizes Europe over migration in D-Day speech
cards.teaser: The US defense secretary spoke in Normandy on the 82nd anniversary of the Allied invasion.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used a D-Day commemoration ceremony in Normandy to criticize Europe's handling of migration. Speaking at the 82nd anniversary of the Allied landing, Hegseth characterized the situation as an invasion of migrants on European beaches and warned that Europe faced invasion by dangerous ideologies.

The speech brought political commentary to a ceremony traditionally dedicated to honoring the World War II Allied operation that liberated Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe. Hegseth traveled to France for the official trip with six of his children.

cards.headline: Pope Leo XIV urges Spain to reject polarization during visit
cards.teaser: The pontiff began a seven-day tour of Spain amid tensions with conservative factions over church policies.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV began a seven-day visit to Spain, his first to the country since 2011, by calling on political leaders to reject polarization and seek unity rather than divide populations for political gain. He emphasized the importance of fighting for peace and respecting every human being.

The pontiff made supporting marginalized communities a central focus of his tour. He met with migrants in the Canary Islands and homeless people in Madrid, while also praising Spain's commitment to peace and solidarity among peoples.

cards.headline: Iran says technical staff denied US visas for World Cup after players admitted
cards.teaser: Iranian officials reported the visa denials hours after the US said players could enter the country.
cards.body:
Iranian officials say technical staff have been denied US visas for the World Cup, contradicting American authorities' earlier announcement that Iranian players would be allowed entry. The timing of the conflicting statements has created uncertainty around Iran's participation in the tournament.

The visa denials add another layer to existing tensions between Washington and Tehran. Without access to coaching and support staff, Iran's team faces significant challenges in preparing for and competing in the competition.

cards.headline: Justice Department investigates California election counting
cards.teaser: The U.S. attorneys office in California opened multiple investigations into ballot counting as millions of votes remain uncounted.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors in California announced they are investigating the state's election counting process. The Justice Department sent federal observers to monitor ballot counting in Los Angeles. Millions of ballots remain uncounted in the California governor's race.

The announcement follows allegations of election fraud, though no evidence of wrongdoing has been presented. The slow count has drawn attention to California's vote-by-mail system, which allows ballots postmarked by election day to arrive and be counted in subsequent days.

cards.headline: Former CIA officer accused of creating fake spy program found with gold bars
cards.teaser: A CIA officer discovered with millions of dollars in gold bars at his home allegedly created a fraudulent intelligence program.
cards.body:
A former CIA employee was ordered to remain in jail after being found with approximately 40 million dollars worth of gold bars. Prosecutors say the officer created a fake spy program and stole from the agency. A federal judge denied the defendant's request for release pending trial.

The case involves one of the largest alleged thefts from the CIA by an employee. Authorities discovered the gold bars at the former officer's residence during their investigation. The Justice Department has not disclosed details about how the alleged scheme operated or how long it continued.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former congressman convicted of insider trading
cards.teaser: President Trump issued a pardon to Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman from Indiana who served time for insider trading.
cards.body:
President Trump pardoned Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman from Indiana, who served nearly two years in prison for insider trading. Buyer was convicted of making illegal stock trades based on confidential information while working as a consultant and lobbyist after leaving Congress.

In 2023, Buyer was sentenced to 22 months in prison and ordered to forfeit over $350,000 in illegal gains, plus pay a $10,000 fine. He was released in 2025 before receiving the pardon, which eliminates any remaining criminal consequences from his conviction.

cards.headline: Karmelo Anthony murder trial hears testimony about stabbing at Texas track meet
cards.teaser: A witness in the Karmelo Anthony trial testified about seeing the victim reveal a wound moments after a fatal stabbing at a Frisco school track meet.
cards.body:
Testimony continued in the murder trial of Karmelo Anthony, who is charged with fatally stabbing Austin Metcalf at a Frisco ISD track meet. A witness told the jury he saw Metcalf lift his shirt to reveal a large wound immediately after the attack. Prosecutors presented video footage showing the aftermath of the incident.

Witnesses confirmed statements Metcalf made in the moments following the stabbing. The trial is examining whether the killing constitutes murder under Texas law. The incident occurred during a high school track competition, and the case has drawn attention due to the public setting and the ages of those involved.

cards.headline: California appeals court allows Kars4Kids jingle to continue airing
cards.teaser: A California appeals court ruled that the Kars4Kids advertising jingle can remain on radio and television in the state.
cards.body:
An appeals court in California ruled that Kars4Kids can continue broadcasting its jingle on airwaves in the state. A judge separately found that the charity concealed its ties to Orthodox Jewish summer camps in upstate New York. The ruling allows the organization to maintain its advertising presence despite earlier legal challenges.

The case centered on disclosure requirements for charitable organizations and how they represent their activities to donors. Kars4Kids accepts vehicle donations and uses proceeds to fund youth programs. The court's decision resolves a dispute over whether the organization's advertising violated California consumer protection laws.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth criticizes European migration in D-Day speech
cards.teaser: Secretary of Defense Hegseth used a D-Day commemoration speech in Normandy to attack European migration policies.
cards.body:
US Defense Secretary Hegseth addressed a ceremony in Normandy commemorating the 82nd anniversary of the Allied invasion that liberated Nazi-occupied northwestern Europe. During his speech, he attacked Europe over what he characterized as an "invasion" of migrants arriving on its beaches.

The remarks represented a departure from typical D-Day commemorations, which traditionally focus on Allied unity and wartime sacrifice. Instead, Hegseth's comments centered on current European immigration policies rather than the historical military operation.

hero.headline: Bitcoin Falls Below $60,000 to Lowest Level Since October 2024
hero.teaser: Bitcoin dropped below $60,000, reaching its lowest price point since October 2024 and marking a sharp decline for the cryptocurrency.
hero.body:
Bitcoin's price fell below the $60,000 threshold, sinking to levels not seen since October 2024. The decline marks a significant retreat for the cryptocurrency and has wiped out billions in value from bullish crypto positions.

The drop occurred despite former President Trump's recent embrace of cryptocurrency, suggesting that political support has not been sufficient to stabilize prices. The decline represents one of the roughest weeks for the crypto market in recent memory, with the breakdown of Bitcoin's price revealing ongoing volatility in digital asset markets.

cards.teaser: The semiconductor industry suffered a massive selloff on Friday, wiping out more than $1.3 trillion in stock market value in what marked the sector's worst trad.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Expected to Impact Major Stock Indexes
cards.teaser: The planned initial public offering of SpaceX is set to affect investors in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 indexes.
cards.body:
SpaceX's upcoming initial public offering is drawing significant attention from investors, with analysts examining how the company's entry into public markets will impact major stock indexes. The aerospace manufacturer's IPO is expected to be large enough to influence both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100.

Elon Musk presented details about the offering at an event organized by JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon, generating substantial investor interest. Some analysts have characterized the IPO as dropping a boulder in a kiddie pool, suggesting the offering's size could significantly reshape the market landscape. Industry observers are also exploring connections between the SpaceX IPO and artificial intelligence investment trends.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Discusses Possible Government Stake in AI Companies
cards.teaser: President Trump said his administration will explore the U.S. government taking equity positions in artificial intelligence firms.
cards.body:
President Trump said his administration is exploring deals that would allow the American people to benefit from AI company success. The discussions include the possibility of the U.S. government acquiring equity stakes in major artificial intelligence firms like OpenAI.

Trump characterized the concept as potentially "a beautiful thing." The administration has held talks with OpenAI about structuring a government profit-sharing arrangement, with meetings potentially occurring in the near term.

cards.headline: Paramount Willing to Sell Kids Channels to Secure Warner Bros. Merger Approval
cards.teaser: Paramount has indicated it would divest children's television channels to address European Union concerns about its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery.
cards.body:
Paramount is willing to divest its children's programming channels to address European Union regulatory concerns over its proposed $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. The concession aims to clear antitrust obstacles for what would become one of the largest media combinations in history.

The deal has drawn scrutiny from multiple regulators and consumer groups filing antitrust challenges. Several states are also considering legal action to block the merger. Paramount's legal team is working to overcome these obstacles while defending the combined entity's competitive positioning in the entertainment sector.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Remain Below $200 Despite Major Supply Disruption
cards.teaser: Oil has not reached $200 per barrel even after what analysts describe as the biggest supply shock in history.
cards.body:
Despite experiencing what market analysts are calling the biggest supply shock in history, oil prices have remained well below the $200 per barrel mark. The pricing dynamic has surprised some observers who expected a more dramatic price surge given the scale of the supply disruption.

The relatively restrained price response suggests that factors such as demand patterns, strategic reserves, or alternative supply sources may be offsetting the impact of the supply shock. The situation highlights the complexity of global energy markets and the multiple variables that influence commodity pricing beyond pure supply and demand fundamentals.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Structures SpaceX Compensation to Avoid Tesla Pay Dispute Issues
cards.teaser: Musk designed his SpaceX compensation package with stronger legal protections following controversies over his Tesla pay arrangement.
cards.body:
Elon Musk has structured his SpaceX compensation agreement with enhanced legal safeguards after facing disputes over his Tesla pay package. The new arrangement, which could be worth up to $1 trillion if Mars mission goals are achieved, includes provisions designed to withstand potential legal challenges.

Musk now dominates the list of highest-paid chief executives according to recent compensation data. His approach to executive pay has become a subject of broader discussion about CEO compensation trends, with analysts examining how Musk is reshaping norms around executive pay structures and performance-based incentives in corporate America.

hero.headline: OpenAI launches Lockdown Mode to defend against prompt injection attacks
hero.body:
OpenAI Delays Adult Mode for ChatGPT, Faces Internal Criticism Over Pentagon Deal

OpenAI has postponed the launch of "adult mode" for ChatGPT, shifting focus to what the company considers more urgent priorities. The delay comes as the startup manages competing demands from users, investors, and its own workforce.

Sam Altman announced last October that OpenAI would allow adult content on ChatGPT and implement age verification systems. The company has now reversed course on that timeline. "We're pushing out the launch of adult mode so we can focus on work that is a higher priority for more users right now, including gains in intelligence, personality improvements, personalisation, and making the experience more proactive," OpenAI said in a statement.

The company, which has more than 900 million ChatGPT users, acknowledged the principle behind the original plan. "We still believe in the principle of treating adults like adults, but getting the experience right will take more time," the statement continued.

Instead of rolling out adult mode, OpenAI is implementing age prediction tools that identify users under 18. When underage users are detected, stricter safety settings activate automatically, limiting exposure to graphic violence and sexual content. In the UK, if ChatGPT generates pornographic images deemed illegal under the Online Safety Act, OpenAI must use age verification to prevent minors from accessing that material.

The shift in priorities reflects pressure Altman has faced since declaring a "code red" to improve ChatGPT. The startup is competing intensely with Google, Anthropic, and other AI companies developing rival systems.

The delay announcement comes as OpenAI navigates internal dissent over a recently announced Pentagon contract. Caitlin Kalinowski, head of hardware in OpenAI's robotics division, resigned over the partnership, citing concerns about mass surveillance and autonomous weapons development.

"AI has an important role in national security. But surveillance of Americans without judicial oversight and lethal autonomy without human authorization are lines that deserved more deliberation than they got," Kalinowski wrote on X.

Kalinowski emphasized her objection centered on execution speed. "To be clear, my issue is that the announcement was rushed without the guardrails defined. It's a governance concern first and foremost. These are too important for deals or announcements to be rushed," she added.

OpenAI had moved quickly with the Pentagon contract after Anthropic, the previous AI contractor, was dropped from the position. Altman later acknowledged the deal appeared "opportunistic and sloppy."

Following the resignation and criticism, OpenAI amended its Pentagon agreement to explicitly exclude domestic mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. An OpenAI spokesperson stated the company believes the updated agreement creates a responsible path for national security applications of AI while maintaining clear boundaries.

"We recognise that people have strong views about these issues and we will continue to engage in discussion with employees, government, civil society and communities around the world," the company said.

cards.headline: Apple prepares Siri overhaul and AI updates for WWDC 2026
cards.teaser: Apple's developer conference will showcase a revamped Siri and updates to Apple Intelligence features.
cards.body:
Apple is preparing to unveil a significant overhaul of Siri alongside updates to its Apple Intelligence features at the upcoming Worldwide Developers Conference. The conference represents a major opportunity for the company to showcase progress in artificial intelligence after competitors have dominated headlines with their AI advancements.

The Siri revamp has been highly anticipated as Apple works to modernize its voice assistant, which has faced criticism for falling behind competitors in capabilities and conversational abilities. The updates to Apple Intelligence will demonstrate how the company integrates AI features across its ecosystem while maintaining its focus on privacy and on-device processing.

cards.headline: White House AI advisor Sriram Krishnan departs administration
cards.teaser: Krishnan is leaving his White House position and reportedly plans to launch a new institution focused on AI policy.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan has left his role as AI advisor in the White House. His departure comes as the administration continues to shape federal policy around artificial intelligence development and regulation.

Krishnan reportedly plans to start a new institution that will continue to influence the Trump administration's AI policy from outside government. The move suggests he will remain involved in shaping federal approaches to AI governance and regulation even after leaving his official position.

cards.headline: Trump administration considers taking equity stake in OpenAI
cards.teaser: President Trump said he is discussing deals that would allow the American people to benefit from AI success.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump said his administration is discussing deals that would let Americans benefit from the success of artificial intelligence companies. The comments indicate the government is exploring taking an equity stake in OpenAI, a leading AI developer.

Such an arrangement would be an unusual government intervention in the private tech sector, positioning the U.S. as a shareholder in a major AI company rather than simply a regulator. Trump's framing suggests the goal is ensuring Americans share in economic gains from AI development.

cards.headline: Sea star populations show baby boom after massive die-off
cards.teaser: A biologist observing sea star recovery found a surprising surge in young sea stars following widespread deaths.
cards.body:
Biologists monitoring sea star populations have observed a surprising baby boom following a massive die-off that devastated populations along the coast. The recovery suggests the species may be rebounding faster than expected after the catastrophic decline.

The original die-off raised concerns about the long-term viability of sea star populations and the broader marine ecosystems they support. The unexpected surge in young sea stars offers hope that these keystone species can recover, though scientists continue to monitor whether the rebound will be sustained.

cards.headline: New social apps emerge as alternatives to Instagram
cards.teaser: A next generation of social platforms focuses on interests, creativity, and community rather than algorithmic feeds.
cards.body:
A new generation of social applications is challenging Instagram and other Big Tech platforms by prioritizing interests, creativity, and community connections. These apps take a different approach to social networking, moving away from the algorithm-driven feeds that dominate established platforms.

The shift reflects growing user demand for social media experiences centered on shared interests and creative expression rather than passive consumption of algorithmically curated content.

cards.headline: Ancient microbes preserved with Ötzi the Iceman remain viable
cards.teaser: Some microbes frozen with the 5,300-year-old mummy are still capable of growth after millennia.
cards.body:
Scientists discovered that ancient microbes preserved alongside Ötzi the Iceman are still growing after being frozen for over 5,000 years. The finding raises questions about the nature of preservation and the boundaries between artifact and living ecosystem.

Ötzi, the naturally mummified body discovered in the Alps in 1991, has provided researchers with unprecedented insights into Copper Age life. The discovery that microbes associated with the body remain viable adds another dimension to understanding what the mummy represents, blurring the line between a preserved human specimen and a complex biological ecosystem frozen in time.

hero.headline: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
hero.body:
Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva captured her first Grand Slam championship with a victory in the French Open women's final. The teenage player thanked her coach, her team, and herself after claiming the trophy at Roland Garros.

Andreeva reflected on her path to the title as a journey marked by dedication and personal accountability. She expressed gratitude to her support system while emphasizing the importance of her own commitment to reaching this milestone.

The victory represents a breakthrough moment for the young Russian, who becomes one of the youngest Grand Slam champions in recent tennis history. Her win at the French Open, played on the clay courts of Roland Garros, marks her as a rising force in professional tennis.

The championship comes after years of development in junior and professional circuits. Andreeva has been competing at the highest levels of tennis as a teenager, and this Grand Slam victory validates her potential as a future star of the sport.

The French Open title adds Andreeva to the list of teenage Grand Slam champions and signals a potential shift in the competitive landscape of women's tennis. Her performance throughout the tournament demonstrated the skill and composure needed to win at the sport's highest level.

cards.headline: Kimi Antonelli takes pole position at Monaco Grand Prix
cards.teaser: Ferrari driver Kimi Antonelli secured pole position for the Monaco Grand Prix, edging out Max Verstappen with Lewis Hamilton qualifying third.
cards.body:
The 19-year-old Mercedes driver claimed pole position at Monaco with a flawless qualifying lap, edging out Red Bull's Max Verstappen by just 0.043 seconds. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton finished third. Antonelli's performance was particularly impressive given he faced competition from two drivers with 11 world titles between them on what is widely considered the toughest single-lap challenge of the season.

The qualifying session proved dramatic and intense beneath the tight confines of the Monte Carlo street circuit. With overtaking nearly impossible at this venue, grid position on Saturday effectively determines the race outcome, making Antonelli's pole position crucial heading into Sunday's Grand Prix.

cards.headline: Chicago Bears advance stadium project in Hammond, Indiana
cards.teaser: The Chicago Bears voted to move forward with a stadium project in Hammond, Indiana, and announced they will not change the team's name despite the relocation.
cards.body:
The Chicago Bears voted to advance plans for a new stadium in Hammond, Indiana, marking a significant step in the franchise's move from Illinois. The team confirmed it will retain the Chicago Bears name despite relocating to a new state.

The announcement follows years of negotiations with Illinois officials over potential stadium sites. Illinois lawmakers reacted to the decision, with some expressing frustration over the tactics used during the extended negotiation process. The stadium project represents a major shift for the NFL franchise and the regional sports landscape.

cards.headline: United States falls 2-1 to Germany in World Cup warm-up match
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team lost 2-1 to Germany in their final tune-up match before the 2026 World Cup, with Robinson scoring for the Americans.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team lost 2-1 to Germany in their final World Cup preparation match on Saturday at Soldier Field in Chicago. Antonee Robinson scored the Americans' only goal in the Coca-Cola Send-Off Match, played before a sellout crowd of 63,636.

The defeat concludes the USMNT's pre-tournament preparation before they open World Cup play on June 12 against Paraguay. Germany secured the victory in the friendly matchup at the historic Chicago venue.

cards.headline: Exeter defeats Saracens to reach Premiership playoffs, ending McCall era
cards.teaser: Exeter beat Saracens 32-12 to secure a Premiership playoff semifinal berth and bring an end to Mark McCall's tenure as Saracens head coach.
cards.body:
Exeter defeated bitter rivals Saracens 32-12 to secure a Premiership playoff semifinal spot. The victory marked a significant moment for the Chiefs, who return to the top four for the first time since 2021. Exeter will face Bath at the Rec in next Saturday's semifinal.

The result also ended Mark McCall's 15-year tenure as Saracens head coach. McCall's final match did not go according to plan, with his side unable to match Exeter's physicality and endurance as the game progressed.

cards.headline: Richard Childress says Kyle Busch was set to return to RCR in 2027
cards.teaser: Richard Childress revealed that Kyle Busch was planning to return to Richard Childress Racing in 2027, with the team owner intending to announce the extension at Michigan.
cards.body:
Richard Childress disclosed that Kyle Busch had been scheduled to return to Richard Childress Racing for the 2027 season. The team owner had planned to reveal the contract extension at Michigan Speedway.

Childress made his first public appearance in Michigan since Busch's death, addressing the planned announcement that never came. Austin Hill will continue driving the No. 33 car for Richard Childress Racing in 2026. The revelation offers insight into Busch's career plans and the trajectory that RCR had mapped out before the driver's passing.

cards.headline: NCAA denies Texas Tech appeal to reinstate quarterback Brendan Sorsby
cards.teaser: The NCAA rejected Texas Tech's appeal seeking to restore Brendan Sorsby's eligibility, leaving the quarterback to prepare for the NFL supplemental draft.
cards.body:
The NCAA denied Texas Tech's appeal attempting to reinstate quarterback Brendan Sorsby's college eligibility. The decision leaves Sorsby without a path to return to college football and preparing to enter professional football through the supplemental draft.

Sorsby is now focused on joining the NFL months after the traditional 2026 draft concluded. The supplemental draft offers players who missed the regular draft process an opportunity to join NFL teams. The quarterback's move to professional football comes as a result of the eligibility ruling that prevents his return to Texas Tech.

hero.headline: Anthony Head, Actor Known for Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso, Dies at 72
hero.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles on Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He passed away peacefully from complications due to pneumonia, surrounded by his family, according to a statement from his daughters Emily and Daisy Head.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," they said.

Head portrayed the librarian and mentor Giles throughout Buffy the Vampire Slayer's seven-season run from 1997 to 2003, alongside Sarah Michelle Gellar. The role made him a beloved figure among fans of the supernatural drama series. Sarah Michelle Gellar paid tribute to her former co-star on Instagram, beginning with a quote from her Buffy character: "Tell Giles I figured it out and I'm ok." She continued, "Well I don't have it figured out and I'm not ok. But I know I'm the lucky one because I knew you."

Born in Camden, London, Head was raised by artistic parents. His father founded Verity Films, a documentary production company, while his mother was an actor who played Madame Maigret in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother was also an actor known for his lead role in 1971's Sunday Bloody Sunday.

Head began his professional career on stage, starring in the 1978 West End revival of Godspell. Throughout the 1980s, he appeared in various projects including the 1981 adaptation of Lady Chatterley's Lover and A Prayer for the Dying, which featured Bob Hoskins and Liam Neeson. He also performed as Freddie Trumper in the original West End production of the Abba musical Chess and played Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the 1990 West End production of The Rocky Horror Show.

Head gained significant recognition in the UK and US for his role in Nescafe Gold Blend television advertisements during the 1980s, which featured a slow-burn courtship between a British couple.

During Buffy's production, Head commuted between Los Angeles and England, where his partner Sarah and their two young daughters lived. The production team adjusted his schedule to allow him to return home every three or four weeks.

After Buffy ended in 2003, Head took a recurring role in the BBC sketch show Little Britain, where he played a British prime minister. He also appeared in the BBC production of Merlin and the film The Inbetweeners Movie. More recently, he played former football club owner Rupert Mannion in Apple TV Plus's Ted Lasso, where he starred alongside Jason Sudeikis.

His daughters said in their statement that Head "loved his job very much" and considered himself "incredibly lucky to have been able to work alongside such exceptionally talented people."

cards.headline: Patrick Godfrey, Actor Who Played Leonardo da Vinci in Ever After, Dies at 93
cards.teaser: Patrick Godfrey, an English actor known for portraying Leonardo da Vinci in the 1998 film Ever After: A Cinderella Story, has died at age 93.
cards.body:
Patrick Godfrey, the English actor best known for portraying Leonardo da Vinci in the 1998 fantasy film "Ever After: A Cinderella Story," has died at 93. His death was announced on June 5 by his talent agency, Markham Froggatt Irwin.

Godfrey had a lengthy career spanning British theater, film, and television. He appeared alongside Drew Barrymore in "Ever After: A Cinderella Story," which became one of his most recognized roles.

cards.headline: A24 Horror Film Backrooms Becomes Studio's Highest Grossing Movie at Global Box Office
cards.teaser: Backrooms is crossing $100 million domestically and becoming A24's highest grossing film ever at the global box office.
cards.body:
The horror film Backrooms, directed by Kane Parsons, has surpassed $100 million at the domestic box office and is now A24's highest grossing movie worldwide. The film originated from a popular YouTube horror concept and has rewritten expectations for the studio's commercial potential.

The success of Backrooms marks a shift for A24, traditionally known for critically acclaimed independent films with modest box office returns. The film's popularity demonstrates how online content can translate to mainstream theatrical success.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Releases New Song for Toy Story 5 Featuring Character Jessie
cards.teaser: Taylor Swift released a song for the upcoming Toy Story 5 film that focuses on the character Jessie and has broken several streaming records.
cards.body:
Swift's new track for Toy Story 5, titled "I Knew It, I Knew You," focuses on Jessie, the cowgirl character from the franchise. The song marks a return to Swift's pop country roots and showcases handcrafted care reminiscent of her musical origins. In discussing the song, Swift acknowledged Randy Newman's legendary work on previous Toy Story films, recognizing his creation of the franchise's musical world.

The music video stars Jessie and carries a nostalgic tone connected to the beloved series. The song has resonated with fans as a reminder of what they appreciate about Swift's artistry.

cards.headline: Netflix Announces Ghostbusters: Night Shift Animated Series for 2027
cards.teaser: Netflix and Sony Animation revealed the title and logo for a new Ghostbusters animated series coming in 2027.
cards.body:
The series, titled Ghostbusters: Night Shift, will debut on Netflix in 2027. The streaming service and Sony Animation announced the title and released logo artwork for the upcoming show.

The animated series represents a return of the Ghostbusters franchise to television. Netflix is partnering with Sony Animation to produce the series, which expands the franchise into new animated content.

cards.headline: The Cure Performs Rare Songs at First Concert Since November 2024
cards.teaser: The Cure played deep cuts including 2 Late, Wrong Number, and Mint Car during their headlining set at Primavera Sound.
cards.body:
Robert Smith and The Cure headlined Primavera Sound, marking their first concert since November 2024. The band performed a mix of rare tracks and familiar hits during the set.

The performance included deep cuts such as "2 Late," "Wrong Number," and "Mint Car," showcasing material beyond their most well-known songs.

cards.headline: Peter Phillips, King Charles' Nephew, Marries NHS Nurse Harriet Sperling
cards.teaser: Senior British royals attended the wedding of Peter Phillips, son of Princess Anne, to NHS nurse Harriet Sperling.
cards.body:
Peter Phillips, nephew of King Charles and son of Princess Anne, married Harriet Sperling in a ceremony attended by senior members of the British royal family. Sperling works as a nurse in the National Health Service.

Sperling wore a vintage diamond and pearl tiara for the wedding. Phillips' teenage daughters from a previous marriage took center stage during the ceremony.

hero.headline: Trump pardons former GOP congressman convicted of insider trading
hero.body:
President Donald Trump issued a full pardon for Steve Buyer, a former Indiana Republican congressman who was convicted of insider trading in 2023. The pardon clears Buyer of criminal charges related to stock trades he made using confidential information.

Buyer, who represented Indiana in the House of Representatives, was found guilty of securities fraud after prosecutors proved he traded stocks based on inside information about corporate mergers. The conviction resulted in prison time and marked a significant fall for the longtime Republican lawmaker who had served in Congress for nearly two decades.

The pardon is the latest in a series of clemency actions by Trump targeting political allies and former Republican officials. Presidential pardons erase federal convictions and restore civil rights, though they cannot undo state-level charges or civil penalties that may have been imposed alongside criminal sentences.

Buyer's legal team had previously argued for leniency, though the specifics of their clemency petition were not made public. The pardon power, granted to presidents under the Constitution, allows the chief executive to grant clemency without approval from Congress or the courts.

The decision adds Buyer to a growing list of individuals pardoned by Trump during this term. Presidential pardons have historically generated controversy when issued to political associates or individuals with connections to the administration, raising questions about the appropriate use of executive clemency powers.

cards.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors in Los Angeles have opened an investigation into election fraud allegations in California.
cards.body:
The Los Angeles U.S. attorney's office has launched an investigation into election fraud in California's elections, according to an announcement made as the state's primary races continue to be counted.

The probe follows criticism from conservatives, including President Trump and former Speaker Kevin McCarthy, who have raised questions about California's vote-counting process. McCarthy expressed concerns that California voters were losing confidence in the election process as results continued to arrive from the primary.

cards.headline: Pence says violent Jan. 6 rioters pardoned by Trump should not receive compensation
cards.teaser: The former vice president argued that Capitol rioters who attacked police or vandalized property should not be pardoned or compensated.
cards.body:
Former Vice President Pence said Jan. 6 rioters who assaulted police officers, vandalized government property or sought to disrupt certification of the 2020 presidential election should not be pardoned by President Trump and should never get a dime. He made the comments during an interview on HBO's Real Time.

Pence's remarks address ongoing debate over Trump's handling of clemency for individuals involved in the 2021 Capitol attack. The former vice president was presiding over the electoral vote certification when rioters breached the building, forcing him and lawmakers to evacuate.

cards.headline: Top Trump AI adviser Sriram Krishnan to leave White House
cards.teaser: A central figure in the administration's artificial intelligence policy will depart but may continue influencing technology strategy.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, who has been central to the Trump administration's AI efforts, will leave the White House. Krishnan has played a key role in shaping the administration's approach to artificial intelligence policy and regulation.

Despite his departure from the White House, Krishnan will probably continue to play an active role in the administration's approach to the technology. The transition suggests a shift in how the administration engages with technology advisers, potentially moving expertise outside formal government positions.

cards.headline: McCarthy criticizes California vote count after Trump fraud claims
cards.teaser: The former House Speaker echoed unsubstantiated allegations about California's election process as primary results continue.
cards.body:
Former Speaker Kevin McCarthy criticized California's vote-counting process, joining other conservatives in questioning the state's election integrity. McCarthy's comments echoed claims made by President Trump, who accused California Democrats of "trying to steal" the gubernatorial and Los Angeles mayoral elections.

California's slow ballot count has drawn scrutiny as mail-in votes continue to be processed and verified. Election experts say the state's deliberate counting process is designed to protect against fraud and ensure every vote is counted accurately. The Justice Department sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles amid the ongoing count.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary as votes are counted
cards.teaser: Early results show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra ahead in the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
The latest California governor primary results show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra leading their respective party races. Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer and Becerra are competing for the Democratic nomination, while Republicans Chad Bianco and Hilton vie for the GOP slot.

The primary will determine who advances to replace Governor Gavin Newsom in the general election. California uses a top-two primary system, though party nominations remain significant for organizing campaign resources and party support heading into the fall contest.

cards.headline: Former Biden official Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: The former Interior Secretary could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the New Mexico Democratic primary for governor. The former Interior Secretary and congressional representative will advance to November's general election, where she will face the Republican nominee.

If elected, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in the United States.
